Preventive or corrective maintenance task on a building, facility, or workplace asset (HVAC, lighting, doors, plumbing, janitorial, grounds). REAL-EST-mastered; FSM consumes/contributes via handoff. Distinct from EAM `eam_work_orders` (industrial plant/equipment) and FLEET-MAINT `vehicle_work_orders` (fleet vehicles).
Geographical field / paddock boundary record with soil-type, productivity zones, and crop-history; the spatial unit of farm operations.
Branded farm e-commerce storefront configuration: catalog scope, member-only pricing tiers, gift-card setup, mobile UX skin.
On-site farmers-market transaction or reconciliation summary; SKU-level line items, tender mix (cash / card / EBT-SNAP).

Pre-check legally required disclosure form presented to the candidate before any consumer report is requested. Carries the disclosure text version, candidate acknowledgment signature, timestamp, and jurisdiction-specific addenda (CA, NY, etc.).

Candidate acknowledgment of receipt of the FCRA Summary of Consumer Rights at consent time, prior to a background check. Required by 15 U.S.C. §1681g(c). Captured separately from the consent itself so the disclosure copy and acknowledgment timestamp persist for audit.
21 CFR Part 11 audit trail row for GxP-relevant training; tamper-evident, retention-locked.
Customer request for new capability; input to the prioritization workflow.

Versioned feature-store entry: feature definitions, materialization logic, online/offline serving configuration, freshness SLA, and lineage to source tables. The intermediate artifact between raw data and trained models.
Per-group TMR (total mixed ration) formulation: ingredients, inclusion %, mixing log; income-over-feed-cost calculation.
Continuous-feedback artifact: kudos, 1-on-1 notes, requested feedback, peer comments. Independent of formal cycle structure; aggregated into performance_reviews summaries.
Per-pass chemical / fertilizer / micronutrient application event with product, rate, applicator, restricted-use justification.

A scheduled or completed on-site visit by a field technician. Captures arrival, departure, work performed, parts used, customer signature, outcome. Distinct from work_orders (the demand-side artifact); a single work_order may produce multiple field_visits if the work spans days or requires re-dispatch.

Approved annual or quarterly budget by org unit, cost center, account, and period. Once approved, drives spend authorization downstream (procurement, headcount, capex). Plan-vs-actual variance is the operational output.

Rolling forecast records (typically monthly or quarterly refresh): updated view of expected revenue, cost, and headcount given current actuals. Distinct from the static budget. Refreshing forecasts upstream of SWP triggers workforce plan re-alignment.

Umbrella entity for financial planning artifacts: annual budget, rolling forecast, long-range plan (LRP). Carries planning period, version, approval state, and pointers to the line-item budgets, forecasts, and variances that compose it. Consumes workforce_cost_projections from SWP for the people-cost line.

What-if financial models layered on top of a base plan: revenue upside / downside cases, cost-cutting scenarios, M&A scenarios. Mirrors the structure of SWP's workforce_scenarios for the financial dimension; the two are usually linked via the cost projection.
FINRA Rule 1240 continuing-education ledger row per registered representative; regulator-evidence retention.
Computed match between a person and a role or opportunity, with score, model version, drivers.
Capitalized property/plant/equipment record: acquisition date, cost basis, useful life, depreciation method, location, status. Distinct from operational hardware_assets (CMDB/HAM).
Time-bound assignment of a vehicle to a driver, a route, or a job; carries start/end time, purpose, expected mileage.

Person authorized to operate fleet vehicles: license class and expiration, medical card status, training/certifications, employer (employee or contractor), HOS status. Multi-master with `employees` for employed drivers; contractors are driver-only.
Fleet vehicle master record: VIN, make/model/year, registration, fuel type (ICE/EV/hybrid), in-service date, assigned base/depot, current lifecycle status. The anchor of fleet management.
Floor layout, desk/room locations, capacity, zone assignments.
A computed measurement of flow (velocity, time, load, efficiency, or distribution) for a value stream over a period, derived from mirrored work items.
A configured definition of a flow metric and its thresholds and targets, against which measured flow is evaluated.
Remediation tracking: owner, target date, evidence upload, closure date. Closure → closes corresponding GRC issue.
Deviation, complaint, or non-conformance event triggering investigation and corrective / preventive action (CAPA).
Historical comparison of submitted forecasts against actual closed results, used to measure forecast accuracy and train the forecasting models.
A manager override applied to a submitted forecast, capturing the changed number and the rationale for the adjustment.
A rep or manager submission for a forecast period, moving from draft to submitted to locked as the forecast cadence closes.
A targeted announcement sent to a frontline audience, with optional mandatory-read requirement, scheduled or supervisor-cascade delivery, and read/acknowledgment tracking.
A reusable template of ordered task items (opening, closing, audit, compliance) instantiated against a location and shift for frontline execution.
A per-worker record that a frontline learning module was completed, with score or pass status where the module is assessed.
A bite-size training unit delivered to frontline workers on a mobile device, with completion tracked per worker and role.
A delivery channel or stream (location feed, team channel, kiosk display, SMS fallback) through which broadcasts and conversations reach deskless workers.
A peer or manager recognition of a frontline worker, delivered in the frontline feed and visible to the team, tied to the recognized worker.
A per-worker submission completing a frontline task or checklist item, carrying the photo, form, or attestation evidence the task required.
A unit of work pushed to a frontline worker or location, completed on a mobile or shared device, with photo or form evidence collected on completion.
A reconciliation record for a fuel tank: opening volume, deliveries, pump totals, closing stick reading, and variance, kept for storage-tank compliance.
A fuel-dock transaction: product (gas or diesel), gallons, pump, price, and the boater or vessel charged.
A bulk fuel storage tank at the marina: product, capacity, and current volume, reconciled against deliveries and sales.
Fuel-card or charging-network transaction: vehicle, driver, fuel type and quantity, cost, location, time. Matched against vehicle assignments for IFTA reporting and exception detection.
Fulfillment instruction group created from order_lines; assigned to warehouse/location, tracked to shipment.
Accounting close cycles for the fund (monthly, quarterly, annual). Drives PCAP statement generation and audit packaging.
Waterfall payout from a real-estate fund to LPs and GP (preferred return, return-of-capital, catch-up, carried interest); calculated on income, sale, or refinancing events.
End-to-end fund-vehicle setup record: entity formation filings, EIN application, banking onboarding, templated LPA. Unique to emerging-manager bundled platforms.
GP-side accounting entries against the fund vehicle (contributions, expenses, fee accruals, gain/loss recognitions) with GAAP/IFRS conformance.
Fund-level performance reporting period: vintage-adjusted IRR/MOIC/TVPI/DPI with PME benchmarking, J-curve normalization.
Per-position return calculation: IRR/MOIC/TVPI/DPI on the fund's holding in a specific portfolio company, time-windowed.
Private-capital fund vehicle (LP/GP partnership structure) with vintage, strategy, target size, and current AUM. The structural backbone every other fund-admin module references.

Court-ordered or agency-issued instruction to withhold from an employee's wages (child support, tax levy, bankruptcy, student loan, creditor). Carries priority, ceiling, remit-to instructions, and lifecycle (active, released, exhausted).
GDPR Article 6 / 7 consent capture for learner training data: purpose, lawful basis, granted timestamp, withdrawal timestamp.
Account in the chart of accounts: code, name, type (asset/liability/equity/revenue/expense), normal balance, statutory mapping. The schema of the books.
Vehicle entry / exit across a defined geofence boundary.
Business-language definition of a concept: term name, definition, steward, domains, related terms, synonyms, certification status. Distinct from ontologies (formal RDF/OWL models).
Confirmation that ordered goods or services were received as expected: receipt date, quantity received, condition. The basis for 3-way matching against PO + invoice that AP runs before payment.
Continuous vehicle location stream (timestamp, lat, lon, speed, heading) — powers heat maps + geofence checks.
A grazing paddock or field: area, location, pasture type, carrying capacity, and rest state. The land unit grazing plans rotate mobs across.
A rotational-grazing plan over a set of paddocks and mobs: planned rotation order, rest periods, stocking rate, and carrying-capacity targets for a season or cycle.
The committed go-to-market plan for a period: the parent artifact that locks and pushes downstream. Mastered by every pure-play planning vendor.
A what-if model of the plan under alternative segment, territory, capacity, or channel assumptions.
Witnessed e-signature binding learner, course, content version and timestamp for FDA 21 CFR Part 11 life-sciences training.
Per-product Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point document: hazard analysis, CCPs, critical limits, monitoring procedures, corrective actions.
Statutory acknowledgment of harassment training completion per CA SB-1343, NY 201-g, IL 2-109; carries signed timestamp and IP.

Physical IT asset: laptop, desktop, server, mobile, network gear, peripheral. Carries serial number, MAC/asset tag, current user / location / room, lifecycle state, depreciation schedule, and procurement reference. The HAM master; CMDB models the same physical thing as a CI for the operational/topology view.
Decommissioning, e-waste tracking, ITAD chain-of-custody and data-wipe compliance for retired hardware.
Canonical catalog of hardware device types, SKUs and specifications; matches assets to refreshable units.
Manufacturer support contract / coverage terms / expiration tracking for a hardware asset.
Field-level harvest projection translated to available-share / SKU planning; drives reserve-list and dynamic pricing.
Per-field and per-zone yield record from combine telemetry, scale tickets, and grain-handling reconciliation.
A scheduled lift of a vessel out of and back into the water using a travel lift or crane, with stands time on the hard.
An identified workplace hazard, its source and affected tasks, and the controls applied to reduce its risk.

Approved slot in the org — a 'chair' with role definition, cost center, reporting line, location, and FTE allocation. Distinct from job_profiles (the catalog definition) and from employees (the person filling the slot). A position can be open, filled, or eliminated. SWP designs future positions via org_designs; HCM operationalizes them once approved.

Period-by-period headcount targets (typically monthly or quarterly) broken down by org unit, location, function, level, and employment type. Includes opening balance, additions (hires, transfers in), reductions (attrition, RIF, transfers out), and target end-of-period count. The basis for plan-vs-actual reconciliation against HCM.
Helm deployment tracking: chart name/version, values overrides, release namespace, installed status.
The headcount plan that closes the capacity gap: roles, timing, and ramp, handed to Recruiting and Finance.

Per-requisition role-scoped staffing junction: assigns specific users to recruiter, hiring manager, coordinator, interviewer, and reviewer roles on a single requisition. Captures team composition without requiring global RBAC for transient interview-panel membership.
Binding between visitor and internal employee host: access scope, duration window, responsible party for visitor supervision.

Employee inquiry or service request routed to HR Operations (pay question, benefits change, policy clarification, leave request, complaint). The HRSD analog of ITSM service_requests, scoped to HR-owned workflows.

A work item generated by a user task in a running process: an assignable, claimable unit of human work with candidate users and groups, due date, priority, and form, completed by a person to advance the instance.
Bucket policy, RBAC assignment, RBAC rule, SaaS role grant, database permission. Infrastructure-level IAM artifact. Distinct from DCG `data_access_policies` (governance policy).
A definition of the best-fit account: firmographics, technographics, and qualifying criteria. Authored here and consumed by the ABM platform for engagement.

Identity-resolution edges: email ↔ device ↔ cookie ↔ login ↔ phone. The graph that turns anonymous interactions into resolved customers. Built up over time from event signals; quality drives every downstream activation. IGA contributes employee-as-customer overlap for B2C-employer scenarios.
Engine-running, vehicle-stationary state change — distinct from trip aggregation.

ML or rule-based model trained to extract structured fields from documents (invoices, contracts, forms, receipts). Carries model_type, training lineage, performance metrics, version, deployment_status. Distinct from MLM `ml_models` (generic ML registry).
Reusable definition per document type: field structure, validation rules, target_system mapping. Distinct from ECM `document_classifications` (taxonomy) and CLM `contract_templates` (assembly).
Validation outcome for an extracted record/field set. Carries validation_rule_id, status (pass / fail / review), exception_details, validator_id (automated / human), resolution_state.
Access review / certification campaign and per-user attestation outcome.
User-initiated access request + approval workflow within an IGA platform.
Business-role / entitlement template provisioned into downstream systems — distinct from Semantius platform roles.
Per-target outcome of an IGA-orchestrated provisioning action (success, failure, retry).
Segregation-of-duties policy violation and exception-approval record.

IGA's governance view of a user's access to an application: the entitlement grant, who requested it, who approved it, when it was last certified, and when it was revoked. Driven by birthright policy plus access-request workflow. Correlates with an smp_license_seat_assignment (the seat/cost view of the same access fact); the two routinely diverge.

In-house legal matter (dispute / transaction / advisory / IP case / regulatory response): client department, opposing parties, matter type, key dates, assigned in-house counsel + outside counsel, budget, status. Scope-qualified to distinguish from law-firm `legal_matters` (id 391, LEGAL-PRACT-MGMT-mastered).
Proactive incident forecast (likely unplanned change → service impact in N hours) — higher-level than per-signal anomaly.

Physical plant, equipment, or infrastructure tracked for maintenance and lifecycle: HVAC units, generators, pumps, conveyors, production-line machines, building systems. Carries asset_tag, location, manufacturer, install_date, criticality, current_state. The EAM master; distinct from HAM `hardware_assets` (IT gear: laptops, servers, network), `fixed_assets` (ERP-FIN capitalization view of the same physical thing), and CMDB `configuration_items` (logical/topological IT view).
An industrial-hygiene sampling or exposure-monitoring result for a chemical, noise, or other agent, measured against occupational exposure limits and linked to the exposed workers and tasks.

Creator/influencer profile managed in influencer-marketing tools: audience metrics, content history, contracts, payments, and campaign attribution. Distinct from contacts (which represent customer/prospect individuals).

Purchase order from the agency to a specific media outlet (publisher, broadcaster, platform) committing budget at negotiated rates with commission terms and make-good provisions. Reconciled against the media outlet's invoice.
A prioritized alert raised when correlated indicators cross a risk threshold for a user. Triaged and dispositioned, and escalated into an insider-risk case when warranted.

An investigation case opened on a suspected insider threat. Carries the full lifecycle from triage through investigation to disposition, the activity timeline, linked evidence, and the HR/Legal handoff.

Customer-owned equipment that the service organization installs and maintains. Carries identity (manufacturer, model, serial), placement (customer_site), and lifecycle state (active, out_of_service, decommissioned). The asset register that work orders are performed against and service contracts cover.
Junction assigning an instructor to a session or offering, with role (primary / assistant / observer).
Instructor master separate from employees; covers internal trainers, contracted SMEs, and external vendor instructors.

Master record from first notice of loss through adjudication and settlement; P&C and life insurance scope. Carries claim type, loss date, reported date, claimant, adjuster, status (open / in-investigation / settled / closed / litigated), gross/net liability. Scope-qualified to avoid collision with HR claims, warranty claims, healthcare claims.

Underwritten contract defining coverage terms, limits, deductibles, exclusions, effective/expiration dates; the contractual artifact a claim is filed against. Distinct from GRC `policies` (control documents) and tenant lease policies.
Vendor connector definition (per third-party application) with auth_type (OAuth / API key / basic / mTLS).
Transformation rule: source_field → target_field, mapping_logic, transformation_type (direct / computed / lookup).
Higher-level orchestration composing multiple pipelines and connectors. Note potential overlap with DATA-AI-PLAT `data_pipelines` — DI lens is integration-tool, DATA-AI-PLAT lens is platform-engine.
Named, versioned template for recurring event-driven flows (recipes, processes, workflows).
Execution log per recipe invocation: timestamp, status, input_id, output_id, error_log, latency_ms.
Event source (scheduled / webhook / database-change / queue) with polling or push config.
A configured source feeding competitive intelligence (news, review sites, web monitors, field reports).
Intent specification — training phrases, entities, resolution rules — drives detection at runtime.

An NLU output record: detected intent classification, confidence, originating utterance, downstream action taken. Decoupled from conversation_transcripts so intent analytics can roll up independently of transcript retention policy.
A captured buying-intent signal for an account or contact, with topic, source, and strength.

A supervisor's quality review of a recorded interaction, scored against an evaluation form, with section and item scores, comments, agent acknowledgment, and a coaching follow-up flag. Moves through draft, scoring, completed, disputed, and calibrated states.
Transaction between two legal_entities of the same group: intercompany invoice, transfer, allocation. Drives elimination entries at consolidation.
Patron-initiated request to borrow material from another library, including routing across sharing partners, shipping status, and fulfillment workflow.
Internal postings covering full-time roles, gigs, projects, stretch assignments, and mentorships.
Reusable interview template per role / stage. Bundles assigned questions, target competencies, recommended scorecard, expected duration. Greenhouse's core authoring unit.
Composition of interviewers assigned to a specific interview, including their role on the panel (lead, technical, behavioral, debrief moderator) and weighting on the consolidated scorecard.
Question bank entry tied to competencies. Carries question text, type (behavioral / technical / situational), competency tags, suggested follow-ups, rubric.
Structured interviewer feedback against a defined rubric: per-competency ratings, written notes, and a hire/no-hire recommendation.
Bookable time window an interviewer has marked available. Drives self-serve scheduling (Goodtime / Modern Hire / Calendly for Recruiting). Carries interviewer, start, end, allowed interview types.
Scheduled assessment event between a candidate and one or more interviewers. Carries time, location/medium, panel, interview kit, and outcome.
A recertification record: an owner attests that a piece of content is current, or flags it stale for remediation or archival.
Derived freshness, quality, accessibility, and ownership-coverage score per inventory record.
A discovered or registered piece of intranet content (page, hub, space, library, form) across connected intranets, with source, type, last-modified, owner, and governance status.
Assignment of an accountable owner and backup to an inventory record, with the review cadence the owner is responsible for.
A governed content-type definition (policy, news post, hub, library, form, FAQ) carrying its default review cadence, criticality, and retention rule.

Scheduled or ad-hoc inventory count session: location, item-filter scope (ABC class, last-counted-before, all), assigned counter, status (scheduled, counting, variance_review, posted), per-line variances.
INV-MGMT-scoped lot or batch identifier: lot_code, item, supplier, manufacture_date, expiry_date, originating receipt. Distinct from FDS `traceability_lots` (FSMA-204 food-traceability scope).
Bill-of-kit for sellable bundles: parent item, list of component items with quantities, assembly_required flag (vs. explode-at-order).
Item by location replenishment policy: reorder_point, reorder_quantity, safety_stock, lead_time_days, preferred_supplier, auto_generate_po flag.
Individually-tracked unit with a unique serial: item, current location, current status (in_stock, reserved, issued, returned, scrapped), warranty_start.
Per-item by per-location quantity record: on_hand, reserved, in_transit, available_for_allocation. Real-time maintained by stock_movements; not directly edited.

Inventory-scoped item record: SKU, unit of measure, lot/serial-controlled flag, ABC/XYZ class, default cost method (FIFO, LIFO, weighted-average), weight, and dimensions. INV-MGMT-mastered for standalone deployments; embedded-masters `commerce_products` when B2C-COMM is canonical.
INV-MGMT's finer-grain location catalog: warehouse, store, bin, zone, or hub. Defers to OMS `inventory_locations` (canonical) when present; deployable standalone otherwise.
Append-only event ledger of inventory transactions: receipt, issue, transfer-in, transfer-out, adjustment-positive, adjustment-negative. Underlies stock_balances; posted movements are immutable.

Inter-location transfer header with lines: source location, destination location, requested-by user, status (requested, approved, in_transit, received, discrepancy, reconciled), expected arrival date.
Stock-location catalog: location_code, type (warehouse / store / 3pl / hub), on_hand, reserved, available_for_allocation. WMS will co-master balances when loaded.
A preserved evidence artifact attached to an insider-risk case (file copy, activity snapshot, screen capture, lineage trace, exported report) with chain-of-custody metadata for HR and Legal review.
Fund entity (name, vintage, size, type, GP, fee schedule, dissolution date) — organizes capital calls + distributions.
Internal IC document per deal capturing thesis, financials, risks, deal-team commentary, and IC vote. Locked at final IC vote.

Real-estate asset held for investment return (acquired/operated/disposed for cash flow and appreciation); carries acquisition basis, debt structure, current valuation, NOI history. Distinct from REAL-EST `real_estate_properties` (the corporate-tenant occupancy view) — same physical asset can underlie both rows in different domains.

People in the firm's external network: founders, executives, co-investors, advisors, LP-side contacts. Distinct from CRM's customer-side `contacts`. The minimum-embedded-shape is the GDPR-relevant subset every module embedding this record must support.

Three-way-match outcome record: invoice, purchase_order, goods_receipt with line-level match status (matched / quantity_variance / price_variance / no_po / exception). Drives auto-post or exception-queue routing.
A candidate's submission against a specific requisition. Carries pipeline stage, status (active / rejected / withdrawn / hired), source, and the full evaluation history.
Formal employment offer extended to a candidate. Carries compensation components, start date, terms, approval chain, and status (draft / approved / sent / accepted / declined / rescinded).
Syndication of a job_posting to an external board (LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor, internal mobility portal). Carries board name, post timestamp, expiry, cost, applicant attribution.
Published, candidate-facing version of a requisition on a career site or job board. One requisition can have many postings (per board, language, or region).

Canonical role definition in the job catalog: title, family, level, responsibilities, required skills and competencies, pay range, FLSA classification. Distinct from positions (which are slots referencing a profile). Many positions share a single job profile.
Approved request to hire for a specific role. The master ATS work item, carries headcount, level, location, hiring manager, recruiter, and status (draft / open / on_hold / filled / canceled).
Individual posting to the general ledger: header (date, source, period) plus balanced debit / credit lines tagged with GL account, cost center, dimension members. The atomic accounting unit.
Sequential node in an experience flow (step 1 → step 2 → exit).
FSMA-204-defined KDE attached to a CTE; sortable into FDA spreadsheet response format.
Knowledge-graph-platform-mastered entities — distinct from DATA-AI-PLAT shared knowledge_graph_entities.
Knowledge-graph-platform-specific ontology. Distinct from DATA-AI-PLAT shared ontologies.
KB content backing both self-service portals and agent-assist tooling. Lifecycle: draft → review → published → retired. Quality and freshness are the silent ITSM KPIs that drive deflection rate.

Authored, versioned content unit. The KMS standalone-market master, distinct from ITSM/CSM/HRSD/LSD bundled `knowledge_articles` (which are platform-embedded). Lifecycle: draft → published → archived.
Hierarchical organization of articles (topics, sections, tags, search facets).
Curated groupings of articles (product docs, process guides, FAQs, onboarding playbooks). Audience tags + expiration.

Typed instances of ontology classes — RDF named individuals or LPG nodes — with assertions, relationships, embeddings, and provenance. The 'data' tier of a knowledge graph that AI agents query and operational apps write back to.
Logged search events for analytics; identifies gaps (zero-result queries).
Cluster resource: name, version, control-plane config, network CIDR, CNI choice, feature gates, API-server settings.

External labor-market overlay used to validate plan assumptions: availability, prevailing salary, time-to-hire, and supply concentration by role × geography × level. Typically sourced from third-party labor-market data providers rather than generated internally; the SWP-side record is the imported/cached view used for planning.
Per-cow per-lactation cycle: calving date, dry-off date, peak milk yield, 305-day projection, days-in-milk.

Registered table or view in the platform catalog, materialized over open table formats (Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi) on object storage or as native warehouse tables. Carries catalog/schema/name, ownership, tags, classification, format metadata, and a pointer to the underlying physical layout. The unit of data on which lineage, governance, BI queries, and ML training all sit.
A cross-functional task within a launch plan, assigned to a function and tied to a milestone.
A dated checkpoint inside a launch plan (kickoff, content-complete, sales-ready, GA).
A working go-to-market plan for a launch: scope, milestones, readiness gate, and owners.
User-built application on the low-code platform: name, owner, deployment, permissions, status. The unit of LCAP delivery.
Custom domain object defined within an LCAP app: schema, fields, references, validation rules, security model. The data layer of the LCAP delivery.
Configured external connection (CRM, database, REST API) bound to a low-code app with schema introspection.
UI screen or page authored as a versioned LCAP application artifact (page, screen, or canvas).
Business process definition inside an LCAP app: states, transitions, role-based steps, integrations, escalations. The behavior layer of the LCAP delivery.

Scoring records per lead/contact — explicit signals (form-fill, demo-request, content-download) + implicit signals (behavior, fit/firmographic match). The mechanism behind the MQL handoff to CRM; thresholds and decay rules drive routing.
Earned-badge junction per learner per badge; carries earn date, evidence URL, and verification token.
Issued credential against a worker (internal certification, vendor cert, regulatory cert) with issue date, expiry, issuing body, and renewal rules. Drives recertification campaigns.
Per-learner sent-notification log row for reminders, nudges, completions, and escalations.
Reusable content asset (video, PDF, image, audio) referenced by lessons and modules.
Path-to-learner assignment row distinct from course_enrollments; tracks overall path progress and completion percentage.
Ordered step inside a learning path: pointer to a course, sub-path, or external resource with sequencing rules.
Curated sequence of courses targeting a role, skill, or certification. Drives ordered enrollment and progress tracking across multiple courses.
Personalized plan composed of multiple paths or courses, often manager-curated or AI-recommended against skill gaps.
Per-learner suggested content generated from skill gaps and role profile.
Granular completion event for a course or activity, often xAPI / SCORM / cmi5 statement: actor, verb, object, result, timestamp. Feeds skill_profiles and certifications.

The lessee lease contract as the accounting subledger record: parties, leased asset, commencement and end dates, term, options, components, and the payment terms the accounting is built from. The lessee-accounting view, distinct from the workplace occupancy record and the landlord operations record.

The classification decision for a lease and its supporting test results: finance versus operating for ASC 842 lessees (and lessor sales-type, direct-financing, operating buckets); single lessee model under IFRS 16. Re-tested on modification.
A tracked obligation deadline on a lease: option-exercise windows, renewal and notice dates, rent reviews, and termination deadlines, with alerting so the obligation is acted on before it lapses.

A prepared lease-accounting disclosure for a reporting period: weighted-average discount rate and remaining term, maturity analysis of undiscounted cash flows, lease cost by type, and the standard reconciliations, frozen once filed.
A source document attached to a lease: the executed contract, amendments, abstracts, and correspondence that evidence the terms feeding the accounting.
The lease liability measured at the present value of unpaid lease payments, unwound with effective interest over the lease term and remeasured on modification or reassessment.

A change to a lease and its accounting consequence: scope or consideration changes, remeasurements, reassessments, discount-rate updates, index and rate true-ups, and right-of-use asset impairment, with before-and-after balances.
The period-by-period schedule of lease cash flows, liability amortization (principal and interest), and right-of-use asset amortization that drives recognition and the maturity-analysis disclosure.
Documented legal opinion / consultation: matter or requestor reference, advice narrative, applicability scope, confidence, expiry/review date, privilege classification.

Court-centric tracking for litigated matters: court/jurisdiction, case number, judge, calendar (filing, hearing, trial, appeal dates), opposing counsel, key documents. Subset of in_house_legal_matters with litigation metadata.

Canonical contract record: counterparty / supplier, contract type (MSA, SOW, NDA, DPA, subscription, lease), effective and expiry dates, total value, governing law, status (draft, in-negotiation, signed, active, expired, terminated). The most multi-mastered SaaS-related object — CLM owns the document, S2P and SMP contribute context.
Statutory company: legal name, registration, jurisdiction, currency, fiscal calendar. Books are kept per legal entity; consolidation rolls them up.

eDiscovery / litigation preservation notice: matter reference, affected record types (email, documents, messages, files), custodian scope, issued date, lifting date. Drives enforcement across data systems.

Demand-signal record: business-unit request for legal advice or service. Carries description, priority, required-by date, requesting department, triage outcome (matter creation / policy guidance / escalation). The front door to LSD.

Law-firm matter (case, transaction, advisory engagement): client, opposing parties, matter type, key dates (statute of limitations, court dates), responsible attorneys, billing rates, status. The central organizing entity of law-firm operations.
Leaf consumable inside a course module: video, document, SCORM block, or live activity.
Order for library materials from a book vendor, including line items, fund allocations, EDI exchange status, and receiving workflow.
Controlled-vocabulary record for a name, subject, organization, or uniform title used as a heading in bibliographic records, supporting consistent retrieval and disambiguation.
Configuration rule defining loan period, renewal limits, fine accrual, and hold behavior for a combination of item type and patron category.
License agreement for an electronic resource (database, ebook collection, ejournal package), including authorized users, concurrent-user limits, ILL permissions, and renewal terms.
Monetary charge against a patron account for overdue, lost, or damaged library items, including assessment, payment, and waiver workflow.
Summary of which copies of a bibliographic record exist at a given location, including coverage statements for serials and shelf-location information.
Patron request to reserve a bibliographic record or specific item for later pickup, including position in queue, pickup location, and trap status.
Physical or digital copy of a work held by the library. One bibliographic record may have many items, each with its own barcode, location, status, and circulation history.
Circulation transaction recording the loan of a library item to a patron, including due date, renewal history, and return status.
Classification of patrons (e.g. student, faculty, staff, public, juvenile) that drives circulation policy and access entitlement.

Registered library member with borrowing privileges, contact information, patron category, and account history. Distinct from platform users; a patron may or may not have a linked user account for self-service.
Patron-owned saved query or reading list in the discovery layer, optionally configured to send alerts when new matching items are added to the catalog.
Active subscription to a periodical or other continuing resource, including issue prediction, check-in records, claim history, and renewal schedule.
Partner library or consortium member with which this library participates in resource sharing, including agreement terms, default lending policies, and contact endpoints.
Book or serials vendor relationship managed by the library, including account credentials, EDI settings, claiming defaults, and contact information.

Audit / true-up record: entitled count, installed count, the resulting gap, true-up cost, and audit-defense evidence. Triggered by vendor audit or proactive internal review. The artifact that justifies a SAM tool's ROI.

Active issued license or permit: license number, holder, type, issue date, expiration date, conditions, jurisdiction, current status (active / suspended / expired / revoked). The post-approval authoritative record.
Renewal application for an existing license: source license, renewal cycle, submission date, updated requirements, fees, conditions changes, outcome. Workflow distinct from initial issuance.

Qualifying event (marriage, birth, adoption, divorce, dependent loss-of-coverage, employment change) that opens a mid-year enrollment window. Triggers benefit_enrollments changes outside open enrollment.
LP entity + commitment + contributions-to-date + governance rights — required for LP compliance (K-1, consent tracking).

An individual head of livestock: identity, breed, sex, birth or acquisition date, current status, parentage, and the mob it belongs to. The animal-centric core record beef and sheep operations build their schema around.

An electronic or visual identifier attached to an animal (RFID / EID ear tag, national-scheme device number, management tag) and the traceability registration it carries. Jurisdiction-gated: the applicable scheme depends on where the operation runs.
A managed group of animals (mob, group, or lot) handled collectively for movements, treatments, and pasture allocation. The unit most day-to-day grazing operations actually operate on.

Borrower request to originate a loan: application date, requested amount, purpose, personal/commercial distinction, loan type (mortgage, auto, commercial line, term loan), requested tenor, collateral, guarantor status, lifecycle state (draft / submitted / approved / declined / funded).

Release of approved loan funds: loan_application reference, disbursement date, amount, tranching (full / phased), destination account, conditions satisfied, regulatory reporting flags. Carries funding state.
Application log stream entries, structured and unstructured. Indexed for search; correlated with metrics and traces for root-cause analysis.

FNOL event giving rise to a claim: occurrence date, location, loss description, cause, subtype (property damage, liability, injury, death), first-reported date. P&C-primary; distinct from ITSM incidents (internal IT operational events).

A customer enrolled in the loyalty program. Captures tier, accrued points balance, enrollment date, opt-in status. Distinct from the broader customers entity (CDP/CRM-mastered): a loyalty member is the program-side identity which may or may not match a CRM customer one-to-one (households, joint accounts, anonymous tier members in pre-identification flows).

A tier definition in the loyalty program (Bronze / Silver / Gold / Platinum or equivalent). Captures qualifying thresholds, benefits, retention rules. The reference catalog every loyalty_member is assigned to.
A point-earning or point-spending event for a loyalty_member: purchase points, bonus-promo points, redemption, expiry, adjustment. The atomic accounting record for the loyalty program.
Active capital commitment from an LP to a fund: committed_amount, called-to-date, distributed-to-date, NAV. The lifecycle record that capital_calls and fund_distributions reference.
KYC and AML output for an LP, including sanction-screening results, captured at subscription time and re-screened periodically.
Limited partners being fundraised — pre-commitment relationship stage. Distinct from `lp_commitments` which is post-close.
LP-facing performance report per fund per quarter: position-level marks, fund-level performance metrics, GP commentary, portfolio highlights. Locked when distributed.
Subscription document collected during LP onboarding: legal commitment to the fund at a stated dollar amount, KYC/AML results, accreditation attestation.
External Learning Record Store endpoints xAPI statements are routed to.
Per-job equipment telemetry log from CAN-bus / ISOBUS / OEM API (planting depth, application rate, GPS track, alarms).
Structured defect / non-conformance record (pre-work-order capture from DVIR or inspection).
Manager-directed reminder triggered when a direct report has overdue or upcoming training.

Manufacturing BOM (mBOM). The eBOM restructured for manufacturing assembly order, with phantom-part rollups, kitting, and process-specific decompositions. The mBOM feeds the MES / production planning system.

Routing master: ordered sequence of operations required to produce a part, with work center, setup time, run time, and resource allocations. Drives MES work-instruction generation and ERP standard-cost calculations.
A mooring ball in a mooring field: position, tackle, weight rating, and assigned vessel.
A wet berth at a dock: number, dock, length/beam/draft limits, utilities (power, water), and service status.
A defined slice of the market (industry, size, geography, motion) the plan targets.
Competitive, pricing, and churn-risk signals aggregated across the conversation corpus, summarizing what the market is saying in aggregate rather than on a single call.
A top-down assignment of budget from a marketing budget to a specific plan line, campaign, or channel, routed through approval and the unit against which spend is reconciled.
A pool of marketing funds for a period, business unit, or region that is approved and then allocated top-down across plans, plan lines, campaigns, and channels.
A shared campaign and content calendar that lays marketing activity out across time, teams, and channels, drawing its entries from plan lines for cross-team visibility and coordination.

Marketing campaign definitions — email blast, drip sequence, multi-channel, paid social tie-in, webinar series, ABM play. Carries target audience (segments), schedule, content variants, attribution settings, performance KPIs.

Email templates and sent instances at marketing scale: list-driven, volume-heavy, branded. Carries open/click/bounce/unsubscribe metrics, deliverability state, sender-reputation impact. Distinct from SALES-ENG `sales_emails` (1-1, rep-driven).
Lead-capture form definitions: fields, mapping to leads/contacts, hidden field rules, conditional logic, post-submit routing (lead score boost, nurture enroll, sales-rep notification).
A plan-level performance or marketing-ROI measure (results, pipeline contribution, return on marketing investment) computed against the plans and budgets that funded the activity.

A line within a marketing plan representing a planned activity, campaign, program, or initiative, carrying its objective, owner, time window, and allocated budget. The grain at which budget is allocated and spend is reconciled.
Annual or quarterly marketing plan: the top-level container that organizes objectives, plan lines, and budget for a marketing period and is approved before execution.

A committed or actual marketing expenditure (purchase order, invoice, or actual) attributed to a budget allocation and plan line, reconciled against allocated budget to compute remaining budget and variance.
Audit record of a matching or scoring batch: model version, inputs (skill profiles, opportunities, roles), outputs (fit scores, recommendations), timestamp.
Decision logic (exact / fuzzy / ML) identifying candidate duplicate records within or across sources; field weights, threshold scores.
Recorded meal and rest-break event evidencing compliance with labor-law break requirements (US state mandates, EU Working Time Directive). Carries waiver attestation where applicable.
Per-campaign media-buying plan broken down by outlet, channel, daypart, audience, flight dates, and budget allocation. Approved media plans convert into insertion_orders.

Medical equipment in clinical use (infusion pumps, ventilators, patient monitors, imaging systems, patient transport). Specialized regulated asset (FDA/MDR, biocompatibility); distinct from EAM industrial_assets (plant) and HAM hardware_assets (IT).
Matched mentor-mentee relationship with goals, cadence, and status.
Defines which source system's value wins per field when two records merge (survivorship: first/last/most-populated/highest-quality/custom).
Periodic compensation review cycle (annual, semi-annual, focal): budget pool, eligibility, calibration step, approval chain, effective date. The recurring operating model of comp management.
Per-employee per-cycle proposed merit increase, bonus, and equity refresh from manager, with calibration adjustments and final approval. Approved values become the pay-rate change posted to payroll.
A positioning and messaging house for a product or segment: pillars, proof points, and approved copy.
A periodic read of a utility meter, manual or wireless, that becomes a billable utility line.

Operator-collected or AMI-transmitted consumption reading: read date, consumption value, unit, read method (manual / AMR / AMI), anomaly flags. Billing-facing time-series at utility scale (millions of reads/day).
Row-level / metric-level ABAC policy at the semantic-definition tier (which BU sees which metric).

Canonical, certified definition of a business metric: numerator, denominator, filters, dimensions, time grain, ownership, certification status, and lineage to physical sources. The atom that the metrics-layer market exists to centralize and govern.
Cached or pre-aggregated metric rollup served from columnar storage by the semantic layer.

Time-series metric streams from instrumented applications — counters, gauges, histograms, summaries. The dev-instrumentation counterpart to ITOM's capacity_records, typically higher-cardinality and tied to release versions.
Bulk-tank or per-cow milk-quality result: SCC, bacterial count, butterfat, protein, antibiotic-residue screen.
Per-cow per-session milking event: parlor / robot ID, milk yield, conductivity, milking duration; from parlor / AMS telemetry.
Training metadata for AIOps ML models (feature set, training window, model version, accuracy, retraining schedule).

Registered machine-learning model with versions, training-data lineage, evaluation metrics, deployment endpoints, and approval state. Backed by the platform's model registry. Distinct from PA's predictive_models, which is the HR-specific attrition-modeling concept consumed inside People Analytics workflows.
A recorded movement of a mob between paddocks, properties, or to an external destination, with date, head count, origin, destination, and reason. Feeds traceability-scheme movement reporting.
App distribution unit: app identifier, version, manifest, app-store link (public store or custom), install silently flag. Distinct from APM `enterprise_applications` (business app portfolio).
AI-generated next-move suggestions for an employee, with rationale and freshness.
An observed insider activity event captured from endpoint, email, file, cloud, identity, or removable-media telemetry. The raw substrate that scoring and detection rules evaluate.

Filtered, human-relevant subset of events that crossed a threshold, matched a pattern, or were enriched with priority and routing. Alerts are what gets paged or ticketed; events are what feeds the correlation engine.

Raw event from a monitored system — state change, threshold crossing, status update, log signal. The firehose, volume-heavy and noisy. AIOPS consumes the full stream for correlation; alerts are the human-relevant subset.
What to monitor, at what frequency, with what thresholds, for which CIs. Often auto-bound to CIs by class via DISCOVERY — a new web-server CI inherits the web-server monitoring policy by default.

An MSP's end-customer organization: site/location hierarchy, contact directory, contract portfolio, and asset estate. The MSP's view of its client roster; distinct from customers (which represent product-company customers in CRM/CSM context).

Multi-flavor service contract between an MSP and an end-customer: block-hour, retainer, value-based, per-device, or managed-services. Tracks consumption, renewal dates, SLA terms, and per-contract billing rules.

Invoice generated by the MSP to its end-customer: recurring service-subscription line items + out-of-contract billable work + tax. Distinct from customer_invoices (SUB-MGMT, software-vendor-issued) and invoices (S2P, AP-side).

Billable service ticket against an MSP service contract: customer tenant, contract reference, time-tracked work logs, billable/non-billable category, SLA timer, dispatch state. Distinct from ITSM-mastered incidents (internal-IT-flavored) — same shape, different buyer and lifecycle.
Per-ticket / per-contract / per-customer technician time entry, with category tagging, billable/non-billable classification, approval state, and downstream feed into payroll and billing.
Third-party store quality assessment (customer experience, compliance, staff courtesy). Distinct from internal store_audits.
Government-issued identity numbers for a worker, such as social security or national insurance numbers, held with restricted access and validity dates. Jurisdiction-specific.
A set of negotiation rules and fallback positions that guide how clauses may be redlined and what concessions are pre-approved.
Historical baseline performance profile (median/p95 latency, loss, jitter) per path/flow/link segment. Used for anomaly detection and alert tuning.
Captured packet/session flows with source/destination IPs, ports, protocols, bytes transferred, duration. The raw observation unit for NPMD traffic analysis.
Physical or virtual network interface on monitored devices (adapters, ports, logical channels). Collection point for flow capture; distinct from CMDB device CI.

Logical/physical network inventory mastered by the telco operator: ports, circuits, IP address blocks, fiber routes, MSAN/DSLAM ports, allocated/free status. Distinct from NPMD network observability (`network_flow_records` etc.) and CMDB `configuration_items`.
Path trace result from source to destination: ordered hop sequence with per-hop latency, cumulative loss rates, RTT. Used for end-to-end path diagnostics.
Threshold breach or anomaly on network performance metrics. Carries severity, affected path/flow, baseline correlation. Network-specific (vs generic OBS alerts).
Time-series of latency, jitter, packet loss, throughput sampled across flows, links, application paths. Primary signal for network SLO/KPI reporting.
Periodic capture of network connectivity: device adjacency, link status, interface roles. Used for topology visualization and root-cause correlation.
Performance × Potential 3x3 grid placement per worker per cycle. Drives succession_plans, high-potential identification, and differentiated investment.
Record-triggered workflow / scheduled job / external API call defined in the no-code platform.
User-defined container for a no-code-database deployment: a self-contained namespace for tables, views, automations, and access.
Public or authenticated intake form authored in the no-code database.

User-defined schema inside a no-code base — tables, fields with types, linked-record relationships, formulas, and views. The 'meta' the platform actually masters; the records themselves are user-owned data the platform stores without owning their semantics.
Switchable presentation layer (grid, gallery, kanban, calendar, timeline) over a no-code base.
Reusable email / in-app / chat template with merge fields, used by automation rules and manager nudges.

Multi-touch outbound nurture flows — branching paths, wait conditions, exit criteria, content trees. The orchestrated counterpart to CDP `customer_journeys`; MA defines, CDP observes resulting behavior.
A learner's scored result against an observation checklist, with observer signoff.
On-the-job competency checklist an observer scores against; field-skill assessment.
Real-time or snapshot occupancy state for a space: desk booked, room reserved, actual check-in via badge/mobile.
A medical surveillance and exposure record such as a respirator fit test, audiometric test, or fitness-for-duty evaluation, retained per occupational-health rules.

Federal-contractor audit log of every applicant-flow event (requisition open, application receipt, disposition, hire) carrying the actor, timestamp, and OFCCP-relevant fields needed to reconstruct compliance decisions during an audit. Immutable append-only.
Approval step in the offer-approval chain (HRBP -> Comp -> Finance -> Exec). Triggered when an offer exceeds band, includes non-standard equity, or matches other escalation rules.
Generated PDF artifact of the offer terms, distinct from the structured offer record. Versioned in lockstep with offer_versions. Carries template_id, render timestamp, e-sign envelope link.

Reusable letter template with merge tokens (candidate name, role, base salary, start date, equity, bonus terms). Versioned. Renders offer_letter_documents at offer time. Carries template name, body, token schema, jurisdiction, language, active flag, and version.

Versioned snapshot of a job_offer during negotiation (initial -> counter -> revised -> accepted). Each version carries the structured terms (base, bonus, equity, start_date) and the author of the change.

Periodic status update on an okr_objective or key_result during the active cycle. Cadence-of-record (weekly/bi-weekly) for OKR programs. May discuss individual performance — flagged as personal content.
Measurable result attached to an okr_objective. The unit of scoring on OKR programs — vendors universally model KR as first-class (Asana, Monday, ClickUp, Workfront).

Hierarchical objective with measurable key results, weighted progress rollup from child objectives or linked work_items, owner accountability, and cadence (quarterly/annual). Mastered by three distinct domains: WORK-MGMT (team-level execution OKRs), SPM (strategic portfolio OKRs), TALENT-MGMT (individual performance-management OKRs). Same primitive, three different lifecycles and review processes — canonical Signal-1 multi-master.

Group of new hires onboarding together (campus intake class, training boot-camp batch, executive cohort, frontline class). Enables shared activities (group orientation, cohort meetings) and cohort-level analytics distinct from the per-journey view.

Record of paperwork collected from a new hire as part of the journey: I-9, NDA, handbook acknowledgment, direct-deposit form, country-specific tax forms, country-specific work-permit evidence. Captures signature state, external e-signature envelope reference ids, and audit metadata. Distinct from the canonical document templates, which would be mastered by a Document Management domain (not yet in catalog).

Instance of an onboarding plan applied to a specific new hire. Materialized when offer.accepted (ATS) or employee.created (HCM) fires. Carries the bound employee_id, assigned tasks, completion state, current stage, and milestone timestamps (pre-boarding start, Day-1 reached, 30/60/90 completion).

Reusable template defining the stages, tasks, timing, and assignees that make up an onboarding journey for a class of new hire (e.g. engineering, sales, executive, hourly retail, contractor). Plans are versioned and selected based on role / location / employment type when a journey is instantiated.
Phase within a plan or journey (pre-boarding, Day-1, week-1, month-1, 30/60/90 day). Defines task grouping, expected duration, and gate conditions. Stages can be sequenced or run in parallel.

Discrete to-do within a journey: sign I-9, attend orientation, complete compliance training, meet buddy, receive laptop. Carries assignee (new hire / manager / IT / facilities / HR), due date, completion state, evidence, and task type (form / training / meeting / provisioning / acknowledgment). Many tasks are local; a subset triggers cross-domain handoffs into ITSM, IWMS, Payroll, LMS, IGA, or HRSD.

Formal model of concepts (OWL classes / RDF schemas / labeled-property-graph schemas), properties, relationships, hierarchies, and axioms. Includes namespaces, prefixes, imports, and constraint shapes (SHACL/SHEX). The 'schema' tier of a knowledge graph.

QBR, MBR, and WBR operating-cadence meeting records. Carries agenda, participants, structured commentary against initiatives and KRs, action items, and outcome summary. Once closed, the record is locked as the audit trail of the cadence.
CRDs + controller deployments (certificate management, monitoring, GitOps controllers, lifecycle operators).
Employee expression of interest in an internal opportunity, with status workflow (submitted, reviewed, accepted, rejected, withdrawn).
Equity pool reserved for employee grants. Tracks pool size, available headroom, reservation workflows, board-approved expansions.
A reusable multichannel play: triggers, audience, channel sequence, and exit criteria.
Inventory-allocation decision per order line across warehouses/stores/3PLs. State: allocated / partially_allocated / backorder_pending. Core OMS function for split orders and cross-dock routing.
Individual product line within an order: quantity, price, discount, tax breakdown. Parent = orders (cascade delete).

Proposed structure changes: new positions, eliminated positions, reporting-line changes, span-of-control adjustments, layer-level redesign. Carries current vs proposed state and the migration path between them.

Node in the organizational hierarchy: division, business unit, department, team. Carries manager, cost center alignment, geographic scope, and parent/child relationships. HCM masters the operational hierarchy; EPM contributes the cost-center mapping (which would be Finance-mastered once a Finance/GL domain is loaded).
The OSHA Form 300 log of work-related injuries and illnesses, maintained per establishment per year, with the annual 300A summary.
The OSHA Form 301 injury and illness incident report filed per recordable incident.

Unplanned loss-of-service affecting one or more service_connections: detection time, cause (storm / fault / equipment failure / load), estimated restoration, affected customer count. Distinct from ITSM `incidents` (IT) and EAM `eam_work_orders`.

One ordered step within an outreach sequence: the channel, the day offset from enrollment, the message template, and whether the step is automated or requires a recruiter action. Defines the cadence the platform follows when a candidate is enrolled in the parent sequence.

Named multi-step sourcing cadence definition (for example day 0 email, day 3 nudge, day 7 message) that automates candidate outreach. Holds the sequence name, owner, channel mix, and active status, and is the parent of its ordered steps.

Engagement with external law firm/counsel: firm, attorney, matter reference, scope, billing arrangement (hourly / fixed / contingent), budget, contract reference, status. Tracks spend and coordination.
Backing service (database, queue, cache, logging) per app: type, plan, provisioning status, plan cost.
Core app record: name, slug, region, buildpack/runtime, git repo, environment variables, domain bindings.
CI-side artifact capture: buildpack output, slug size, build time, buildpack version, env changes.
Activation/release record: app reference, version/commit, build status, release timestamp, deployment status (success / rollback / in_progress), deployer.
Multi-tenancy: dev/staging/prod with env-specific config overrides, resource limits, addon bindings.
Running compute unit (generic process container): type/size, process type, uptime, memory/CPU metrics, status.
An assignment of a mob to a paddock for a grazing period, with start and end dates, stocking rate, and expected versus actual rest. The junction that realizes a grazing plan on the ground.

A scheduled or ad-hoc deployment of OS or third-party patches to a defined set of endpoints, with per-endpoint approval, execution status, success/failure, and rollback state. Tied to maintenance windows and approval workflows.

Scheduled visit between patient and provider: provider, location, scheduled time, visit type (new / follow-up / annual / urgent), status (scheduled / confirmed / arrived / completed / no-show / canceled), reason for visit. Drives front-of-house workflow and resource utilization.

Provider-initiated request for specialist consultation or external service: referring provider, target specialist/facility, clinical indication, urgency, status (requested / scheduled / completed / declined), insurance authorization status. Drives in-network coordination and revenue capture.

A single payroll cycle execution, scoped to pay group, country, and pay period. Drives gross-to-net calculation across the eligible employee population and produces pay_slips, payroll_journal_entries, and tax_filings. The atomic unit of payroll operations.

Per-employee per-cycle gross-to-net statement: earnings, pre/post-tax deductions, employer contributions, tax withholdings, net pay, YTD totals. Called Pay Stub (US), Payslip (UK/AU/IE), Bulletin de Paie (FR), Lohnzettel (DE), Holerite (BR). Worker-portal accessible; legally retained per jurisdiction.
Scheduled batch of supplier payments grouped by bank_account, currency, payment method (ACH, wire, check, SEPA). Drives the AP payment cycle.
Payment attempt / authorization on an order (charge, decline, refund, capture). Multi-state lifecycle; ERP-FIN AR sees settled payments via handoff.
GL posting produced by a pay_run, decomposed by cost_center / department / earning_code / deduction_code into debit and credit lines. The payroll-to-finance handoff payload.
Partner Capital Account statement per LP per close period: contributions, distributions, gains/losses, fees, ending balance. Sent to LPs; submit-locked once distributed.
Card-handler security-awareness training record (PCI DSS 12.6).

Calculated workforce KPIs and metrics: time-to-fill, attrition rate, retention rate, span-of-control, internal-mobility rate, training completion rate, cost-per-hire, time-to-productivity. Derived from HCM, ATS, LMS, Payroll event streams. PA is the master of the calculated KPI definitions and the materialized metric values; source systems master the underlying events.
Individual goal or OKR with owner, period, metric, weight, status, alignment to organizational objectives. Reviewed within performance_reviews cycles.
Per-cycle per-worker review artifact: self-assessment, manager assessment, ratings, narrative, calibration outcome. Drives merit_recommendations and succession_plans.

Citizen or business submission requesting a license or permit: applicant, permit type (building / business / professional / event / environmental), submission date, jurisdiction, supporting documents, fees due, status (submitted / under-review / approved / denied / withdrawn). Scope-qualified to avoid collision with ATS, IDP, banking, healthcare applications.

Field inspection tied to a permit (pre-construction, in-progress, final, complaint-driven): inspection type, scheduled date, inspector, location, outcome (pass / fail / conditional), required corrections, follow-up inspection. Scope-qualified vs CLIN-DEV / EAM / FSM inspections.
A buyer or user persona: role, goals, pains, and buying triggers, referenced by messaging and content.
Context-aware branching logic (IF segment X THEN show variant Y) applied to experiences.
Owner / client relationship for veterinary practice: contact info, payment method on file, communication preferences, household-pet-list, financial-balance history.
Per-recipient outcome of a phishing simulation (clicked, reported, ignored).
Configured simulated-phishing campaign for security-awareness training (PCI DSS 12.6).
A business or technical goal a team commits to for a program increment, scored on planned versus actual business value at the inspect-and-adapt review.
Host-pickup-site, depot, or on-farm pickup point with operating hours, member-self-serve capacity.

Definition of a single attribute available to PIM products: data type, validation rules, attribute group, locale-awareness, and channel-specific overrides. Distinct from runtime attribute values on a product instance.

Hierarchical taxonomy node used to classify PIM products. Multiple parallel taxonomies coexist (merchandising tree, channel-specific trees, ERP category tree); each one's tree lives in this table with a parent_category_id self-reference.

Image, video, 3D model, or document asset tied to one or more PIM products. Carries rights metadata, renditions / derivatives, and CDN-delivery URLs. The DAM slice that lives inside PIM in v1; can be split out to a DAM domain when warranted.

The merchandising-master record for a sellable SKU as PIM models it: a hub of attributes, descriptions, variants, categorizations, translations, digital assets, and channel-specific overrides. Distinct from B2C-COMM commerce_products (storefront runtime view) and PLM engineering_parts (engineering record). Authoritative for marketing / catalog content; consumed by commerce, inventory, CPQ, and marketplaces.

Definition of an outbound publishing channel: marketplace seller portals, merchant feeds, storefront platforms, retailer feeds, GDSN datapools, or a custom partner endpoint. Holds destination-schema mapping rules, credentials, and per-channel attribute overrides.
A single publish run of a product (or batch) to a syndication channel. Carries queue position, run status, per-record validation results, and rejection reasons from the destination.
Locale-keyed string variant of an attribute or description on a PIM product or attribute. Drives multi-language publishing; can be machine-generated, human-translated, or a hybrid pipeline.
Specific size / color / locale / pack-size variant of a parent PIM product. Each variant has its own SKU, can have its own publish state, and inherits attribute defaults from the parent.
Execution instance of a data pipeline: runtime status, lineage snapshot, error state. References `data_pipelines` (DATA-AI-PLAT-mastered).
Sales-process taxonomy: stage definitions, exit criteria, default probability, allowed-next-stage transitions. The configuration object behind the opportunity pipeline.
An append-only record of plan approvals, locks, and the downstream push events.
A saved snapshot of the plan at a point in time, for comparison and audit.
Shelf-layout and product-placement compliance vs corporate planogram standards: deviation, remediation, photo evidence, visual compliance verification.
Per-pass planting event: seed variety, rate, depth, date, weather; ISOBUS-compliant.
CI/CD wired into cluster: GitOps, fleet orchestration, in-cluster build and deploy pipelines.

Resolved configurations of a configurable product: a specific combination of option-and-variant selections that the configurator engine has validated against the 150% BOM and configuration rules. Each variant is a sellable / buildable configuration with its own price, lead time, and resolved BOM.
Staff-augmentation or statement-of-work requisition: scope, role, rate range, duration, location, hiring manager, supplier-tier rules. Drives supplier distribution and candidate submission.
Record that a user read, understood, and acknowledged a policy; timestamp, version, medium, completion evidence.
Individual coverage line within an insurance_policy: line of business, coverage code, limit amount, deductible, coinsurance %, effective period. Determines claim eligibility and adjudication.
ESG and diversity metric submission per portfolio company per reporting period. Drives SFDR Article 8/9 disclosures and LP-side ESG reporting.
KPI submission cycle per portfolio company per reporting period (monthly / quarterly). Captures ARR, headcount, runway, cash, gross margin, NPS, churn.
Fair-value mark per portfolio company per close cycle, per ASC 820 methodology. LP-side valuation distinct from issuer-side 409A valuations.
Investee company held by one or more funds. Carries headline financials, board composition, current ownership %, exit status, sector tagging.
A large body of work in the portfolio backlog that is funded, analyzed, and delivered through a kanban funnel before decomposing into features.
A ship-store retail sale of non-fuel goods, paid at the register or posted to a boater house account.

Projected need for specific roles derived from the capacity model: which positions, when, where, at what level. Feeds the requisition pipeline — approved demand becomes an authorized requisition in ATS via the headcount.approved handoff.

FCRA-mandated notice sent to a candidate before a final adverse-action decision based on a consumer report. Carries a copy of the report and Summary of Rights, and opens a waiting period (typically 5 business days) during which the candidate may dispute findings before the final adverse-action notice issues.

ATS-owned pre-employment record covering the post-offer-acceptance window before the new-hire start date: paperwork in flight, background check pending, pre-boarding tasks open. At start-date the pre-employee row is reconciled into HCM-mastered `employees` (the canonical employee record). HCM owns the canonical employee record; ATS owns the pre-employee lifecycle stage so recruiting and HCM can each move at their own pace.

ML / statistical model outputs deployed in PA: flight-risk scores, performance trajectory, internal-mobility likelihood. Carries the model identifier, training window, target metric, and the materialized scores per employee. Consumes employees and employment_events as features.
Proactive forecast emitted before symptoms surface: predicted capacity exhaustion, predicted failure of a CI based on degradation pattern, predicted SLO breach within the burn-rate window.
Gating logic that controls path progression: required completions, scores, certifications, or competencies.
Per-vehicle-class PM schedule template: trigger basis (mileage / engine hours / calendar time / DTC), task list, due-date generation rules.
Calculation engine: tiered/volume discounts, seat-based pricing, duration-based pricing, bundle discounts, segment overrides.

An activity execution within a process instance: a service task, script, call activity, gateway, or event, with its own lifecycle (activated, completed, failed, compensated) and the job dispatched to a task worker.

Resource-constrained or time-trapped steps in a process: high-wait-time activities, resource queue depth, throughput loss points. Carries activity name, severity, estimated throughput impact, recommended mitigation.

Diagnostic from conformance checking: comparison of event log vs reference process model, flagging deviations with severity, deviation_type (missing / extra / out-of-order / timing), trace-level root cause. Supports regulatory audit.

A deployed, executable process model (BPMN or code-defined) with a unique key and version. Instances are started from a definition; a new deployment publishes a new version while running instances stay pinned to the version they started on.

An append-only record of a single state change in the engine (instance started, activity completed, variable updated, incident raised). The immutable execution history used for replay, recovery, and as the source log downstream process mining consumes.

A blocked execution: a job that exhausted its retries, an unhandled error, or a failed condition that halts an activity until an operator resolves it. Carries the failure detail and the activity it is attached to.

A single running (or completed) execution of a process definition, holding the current token position, scope variables, and a correlation key. The durable, recoverable unit the engine advances through activities and gateways.

A single execution of a process simulation scenario (Monte Carlo or discrete-event) against a business_process_model, with inputs (resource pools, cost/time variables), outputs (throughput, bottleneck nodes), and run metadata.
A typed key-value datum scoped to a process instance or one of its activity scopes, carrying the business payload that activities and gateways read and write as the instance advances.
Distinct execution patterns within an event log: cohorts of traces that follow significantly different paths. Carries variant frequency, average cycle time, actor/resource patterns, business drivers.
As-built record of a manufactured item: serial number, lot/batch, production_order reference, produced_timestamp, quality_status, embedded costs. Traceability spine for batch/genealogy queries.
Reusable package definitions: groups SKUs + mandatory/optional selection rules + bundled-discount rules.

Per part × substance × regulation declaration that asserts whether a controlled substance is present in the part, at what concentration, and whether it falls under a regulatory exemption. Aggregates from supplier declarations and propagates up the BOM via roll-up.
Captures user selections when building a quote line (options on a base SKU mapping to a variant).
Capability / story / epic within a product roadmap. Atomic unit of feature prioritization and customer-to-release mapping.
The long-lived launch record for a product or feature: tier, dates, status, and retro.
Software product line under development and go-to-market. Higher-level than B2C-COMM `products` (SKUs); a product_line bundles features and product_releases over its lifecycle. PROD-MGMT flagship.
KPI tracked over time per product (adoption %, NPS, DAU, feature usage, churn risk).
Versioned software release; bundles features and defines delivery date and scope.
Timeline view of features grouped by release, product, or theme. Marquee PROD-MGMT capability.
Shop-floor equipment/line stoppage: start_time, duration, reason code, impact (throughput loss), resolution. OEE input. Distinct from EAM `eam_work_orders` (maintenance-triggered).
Release-to-floor unit of work: product SKU, quantity, schedule window, build instructions reference, material requirements. Distinct from ERP demand planning; MFG-OPS owns floor execution.
Per-unit/per-batch inspection result: checklist completion, pass/fail, defect classification, produced_unit reference, inspector, timestamp. Feeds quality dashboards and hold/release decisions.

Published build plan for a line, manufacturing cell, or workcenter: time-based slots, assigned orders, sequencing, changeover windows. Product of capacity-planning optimization. Distinct from WFM `work_schedules` (labor-centric).
Summary statistics computed on a data_asset: cardinality, null %, distinct count, value distributions, pattern samples. One per asset per scan.
A fixed timebox during which a release train delivers incremental value, planned in a big-room planning event and closed with an inspect-and-adapt review.
Worker-to-project allocation with role, bill rate, cost rate, planned hours, period. Drives utilization and resource-availability reporting.
Discrete billing trigger inside a project: milestone definition, amount, trigger condition, status. Drives revenue recognition and customer invoicing on fixed-fee engagements.
Forward-looking resource commitment plan (skill, planned utilization %, effective period) — distinct from executed assignments.
Decomposed unit of work inside a project: scope, dependencies, estimated hours, status. Drives time entry tagging and Earned Value calculation.
Markup comment placed on a region of a proof during a proofing session, with the reviewer, location, and resolution state.
Review-and-approval cycle on a creative asset or document attached to a work item. Reviewers mark up the proof and decide approve or request-changes; backs the creative-review capability.
Buyer-side lease contract; terms, dates, financials, renewals. Distinct from `contracts` (CLM) — real-estate specific with ASC 842/IFRS 16 accounting.
Desk, meeting room, parking space, locker, or other allocable unit. Parent = real_estate_property or floor_plan.
Person or household occupying a rental unit under a lease; carries contact info, lease history, payment history, screening result.
Periodic property or portfolio valuation via cap rate, DCF, or direct-comparison method; carries valuation date, method, assumptions, sensitivity outputs. Drives NAV for fund-level reporting.

Code-change proposal targeting a branch in a source_repository: author, base/head branches, title, description, status (open / merged / closed), reviewers, approval count, CI status, merged-at timestamp. The review-cycle artifact.
Bank of survey items rotated through pulse cadence with research-backed driver mapping, anti-fatigue rotation, and benchmarking.
A record of a sewage pump-out for a vessel, kept for Clean Vessel Act grant reporting and state mandates.

Issued PO to a supplier: line items, agreed prices, delivery terms, payment terms, ship-to / bill-to. Authorizes the supplier to deliver. PO creation is a primary trigger for downstream system updates — ITAM gets the asset reference, SMP gets the SaaS subscription anchor.

Internal demand for a purchase: what's needed, who's requesting, justification, budget reference, approval state. The origination point of a procurement workflow; SMP-triggered shadow-IT sanctioning lands here.
Work item raised when a profiling or monitoring rule breaches: root-cause detail, remediation status, linked data assets, SLA.
Business logic defining acceptable data state: cardinality bounds, regex patterns, referential integrity constraints, statistical thresholds. References DCG `data_assets`.
Executed-query audit trail linking metric reads back to source tables, transformations and requestor identity.
Reusable pools of assessment questions independent of any single assessment, drawn from for randomized quizzes and recertification exams.
Real-time and historical metrics per queue: wait time, abandonment rate, service level, average handle time. Drives staffing decisions and SLA monitoring.
Item-level learner response capture for psychometric analysis and per-question review.
An allocated revenue target for a territory, rep, or team for the plan period.
Line- and quote-level discounts: source (rule / manual / competitive), amount, approval status.
Atomic configured-SKU line: unit price, quantity, line total; bundle nesting; line-level discounts and approval gates.
Pre-agreed bill rate by role, geography, and supplier tier. Drives consistent work_order pricing and AP-side three-way match.
A template of cross-functional readiness items a launch must clear before go-live.

Property offered for sale or rent on an MLS or brokerage marketplace; carries pricing, photos, descriptive text, agent representation, and listing-status lifecycle (active/contingent/pending/sold/withdrawn).
Building, facility, or managed space (owned/leased); lifecycle from acquisition/lease-start to sale/expiry.
Deal pipeline from offer through close: parties, terms, contingencies, escrow timeline, and document compliance. One transaction per accepted offer; survives the listing once the offer is bound.

Aggregate session telemetry for an end-user's device over a window: page loads, app launches, network quality samples, DNS query times, VPN toggle state, WiFi/cellular transitions. Distinct from OBS distributed_traces (app-internal) and NPMD (network-internal).
Product recall execution record: affected lots, notification log, hold-and-segregate status, FDA Reportable Food Registry filing.
